patterns.what_worked: Exact action-item subtype and pipeline identity enabled precise routing; staged telemetry windows showed no recent violating endpoints; the existing policy shape supported a one-line normalization.
patterns.what_was_hard: The longest telemetry window initially timed out and required one lower-volume aggregate retry.
patterns.recurring_pattern: Default-deny findings require subtype-aware routing because the same KPI also covers less restrictive feed-isolation scenarios.
patterns.tsg_gap: The metadata-level TSG link emphasized the sibling feed-isolation scenario, while semantic documentation search supplied the authoritative default-deny guidance.
patterns.environment_blockers: Pipeline execution was intentionally not triggered; final confidence depends on developer-run branch validation and subsequent clean-run history.

outcome.changes_proposed: Normalize the targeted pipeline network policy by removing the permissive policy, preserving approved feed-isolation policies, and adding the default-deny policy.
outcome.full_journey: The exact active compliance item and official KPI documentation were retrieved read-only. The action subtype identified the dedicated default-deny path. Recent pipeline telemetry was queried across progressively wider windows and showed no violating endpoints. The specialist inspected the targeted pipeline configuration, created a feature branch, normalized the network isolation policy, and left pipeline execution and calendar-based auto-resolution validation to the developer.
